question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it be community/experimental support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: The codebase has an external FreeBSD package path and some FreeBSD compatibility fixes, but official support would expand the product support contract and release obligations beyond one narrow repair.

options.title: Define community FreeBSD scope
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether to acknowledge the existing FreeBSD ports/pkg path as community or experimental without promising Tier 1 release support.

options.title: Promote toward Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD ownership and open tracked implementation work for installer/update behavior, rc.d service management, docs, CI, and release validation.

options.title: Decline official support
options.body: Close the request if maintainers decide the FreeBSD ports/pkg path should remain external and unsupported by OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Define community FreeBSD scope
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers decide whether to acknowledge the existing FreeBSD ports/pkg path as community or experimental without promising Tier 1 release support.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is the project-wide support contract rather than a single implementation defect.
